properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.configuration
properties.description: The configuration that each endpoint copies as its defaults, before the endpoint options are applied. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.azure.iothub.IoTHubConfiguration type.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.connection-string
properties.description: The connection string of the device, with its HostName, DeviceId and SharedAccessKey. The producer opens one device client per hub, device and module of the connection string, and reuses it; an HTTPS endpoint uses a client of its own. The CamelAzureIoTHubConnectionString header replaces this option.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.content-encoding
properties.description: Content encoding applied to telemetry messages. Set it to an empty value to send telemetry without a content encoding, for example for a binary body such as Avro or Protobuf.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.content-type
properties.description: The content type of the telemetry message, which IoT Hub message routing needs to query the body. The contentEncoding option sets the content encoding.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.delivery-mode
properties.description: What the producer sends. TELEMETRY sends the body as a device-to-cloud message, TWIN updates the reported properties of the device twin, and BOTH does both. The CamelAzureIoTHubDeliveryMode header replaces this option.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.device-client-eviction-interval
properties.description: How often the component checks the pool for device clients that are unused for longer than deviceClientIdleTimeout, and closes them. A value of 0 or less uses 30 seconds.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.device-client-idle-timeout
properties.description: How long a pooled device client can be unused before the component closes it. A client is unused when no producer sends with it. A value of 0 or less uses 5 minutes.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the azure-iothub component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.protocol
properties.description: The protocol of the device client. MQTT_WS and AMQPS_WS are MQTT and AMQPS over WebSocket on port 443. The SDK supports device twin operations only over MQTT, MQTT_WS, AMQPS and AMQPS_WS.

properties.name: camel.component.azure-iothub.send-timeout
properties.description: How long the producer waits for IoT Hub to acknowledge a telemetry message, and for each device twin request: getting the twin, updating its reported properties, and the subscription to desired properties when a device client is created. Opening the device client uses the retry policy of the Azure IoT SDK and is not limited by this timeout.
